provisions.summary: Replaces the tax years 2027 and later income tax schedules with one that raises the top three rates by one point each (to 10%, 11% and 12%) for all three filing statuses, and repeals the scheduled 2027 and 2029 adjusted schedules.

Raises the applicable percentage and the income ranges used to calculate the household and dependent care services credit (50% for AGI up to $80,000, phasing down to 5% above $160,000), effective for tax years after 2026 and reverting after 2032.
Denies the dependent care credit for ten taxable years after a final decision that a claim was due to fraud, and for two taxable years after a final decision disallowing a claim.
provisions.quote: No credit shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year in the disallowance period.

provisions.summary: Moves the repeal of Act 163, SLH 2023 from December 31, 2027 to December 31, 2032, which keeps the EITC at 40% of the federal credit (section 235-55.75(a)) and the larger food/excise credit table (section 235-55.85(b)) through tax year 2032.
provisions.quote: provided that on December 31, [2027,] 2032, this Act shall be repealed

provisions.summary: The same sunset extension also keeps the Act 163 amendments to the dependent care credit dollar limits in section 235-55.6(c) through tax year 2032.

notes: The effective date of July 1, 3000 looks like a placeholder. Section 2 is made applicable to tax years beginning after December 31, 2026. The section 1 brackets are modeled from tax year 2027 on this reading: the bracketed 2027 and 2029 adjusted schedules are repealed, so the unbracketed schedule dated after December 31, 2026 stays in force through 2031 with no later indexing. The Act 163 sunset moves to December 31, 2032, beyond the 2027-2031 horizon, so both credit settings hold for every modeled year. The dependent care credit changes (higher applicable percentages and income ranges, the fraud and disallowance periods, and the section 235-55.6(c) limits) cannot be modeled; the revenue estimate leaves out their cost. The standard deduction, personal exemption and capital gains rate are untouched.
